name: sbcl
why: A high-performance Common Lisp with a live image and REPL, a rich old-school environment worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: SBCL (Steel Bank Common Lisp) is a high-performance compiler and runtime for ANSI Common Lisp. Its homepage describes it as open source free software under a permissive license. Beyond the compiler and runtime, it ships an interactive environment with a debugger, a statistical profiler, a code coverage tool, and many other extensions. It runs on Linux, various BSDs, macOS, Solaris, and Windows. The homepage gives no details on exact inputs or outputs, so the brief does not claim any.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit problem statement. It presents SBCL as a fast, free Common Lisp implementation with a full interactive development environment.
brief.install_notes: The homepage points to a Download page, a Getting Started guide, and a Documentation section, but I could not read them: /getting-started.html and /download.html both returned HTTP 404. The homepage itself gives no install steps, hardware needs, or first-run configuration beyond the list of supported platforms.
brief.standout: SBCL is a native compiler with a live image and an interactive debugger and profiler built in, in a single free package. The homepage pitches it as a high-performance Common Lisp with its own tooling (profiler, coverage) rather than as a bare interpreter.
brief.status: Maintained, per the homepage. It names SBCL 2.6.9 as the most recent version, released September 26, 2026, and links release notes and a Launchpad bug database. I did not see a commit history or a changelog, so this is based only on that homepage claim.
brief.caveats: I could not read the Getting Started, Download, or Documentation pages (404 errors), so install steps, build requirements, and command usage are unverified. The homepage's own description is short and gives no usage examples. The brew scout note calls it a live image and REPL environment; that matches the homepage's description of an interactive environment, but I did not confirm the REPL details on a documentation page.
quotes: SBCL is a high performance Common Lisp compiler. It is open source / free software, with a permissive license.

In addition to the compiler and runtime system for ANSI Common Lisp, it provides an interactive environment including a debugger, a statistical profiler, a code coverage tool, and many other extensions.
The most recent version is SBCL 2.6.9, released September 26, 2026 (release notes).
